For the sake of your sanity and everyone else’s, follow the 3-2-1 rule. 3 hours of sleep, 2 meals, and 1 shower every day as a bare minimum. A lot of people will prefer more sleep than that, so feel free to get more of any of these, but please, for everyone’s sake, don’t get less. The dealer hall does get pretty warm with 40,000-50,000 people, and you will be walking a lot. You think just sitting down and playing games wouldn't burn many calories, but you're also doing more walking than you probably would at work. And please don’t make others suffer due to your poor hygiene. Saturday is notorious for gamer funk candidates; even if you don't think you need a shower, you do.

Have a plan. There are lots of things to do at Gencon and only so much time to do them in. Pay attention to what of your favorite games are releasing stuff limited to the convention and get in line for that stuff as early in the week as possible. If you wait until Saturday when the crowd's the biggest or Sunday when vendors are just getting rid of scraps, you're likely going to miss out. Figure out what you MUST do and then figure out what would be nice to do. Don't over-schedule because you will likely run over time in some events.

Drink water. Yes, the convention center is air-conditioned, but it is also incredibly hot and humid getting to it. I understand the need to caffeinate, especially going into Saturday evening, but hydrate. It will keep alert instead of just being awake.

Start walking now. Unless you are just farming for convention exclusive like Heroclix, you’re on your feet A LOT. If you’re not used to standing and walking all day, I highly suggest you spend 20-30 minutes a few days a week just acclimating your body to some of the physical rigor of the con. Also, make sure you take comfortable shoes. Some people recommend taking two pairs and switching them up, but I’m usually fine with one really good pair.

Take a bag with you. Some people prefer the side-hanging bags so they can easily get into it while walking and as potential theft deterrent. The problem I have with side bags is that there are popular sections of the convention that are crowded and your side bag will be bumping into a lot of things. I plan on bringing a backpack that can store a water bottle and have supplies for random pickup games (dice, cards, some minis, and tablet with Pathfinder sheets.) Unless it is close to an event like the big evening Pathfinder session, don't be lugging around all of your books with you.

Take snacks and eat at weird hours. This one is 100% preference, and is probably not as helpful if you have children, but we always try to minimize downtime. We usually eat at 4 p.m. and then again around 10 or 11 p.m. Sometimes we make a shake run at 3 a.m. during happy hour. The close eateries with ALWAYS be busy, but when we go to Steak and Shake at 4, we usually only have to wait 10 minutes tops for a table. On that note, depending on how hard you want to go, sitting down to eat away from games is such a nice change-of-pace. Gencon is an absolute devourer of time and if you don’t schedule meals, it’s really easy to blow right through them.

This one again is just preference, but get out of your comfort zone a little. Planning is awesome, but if you’re just wandering around looking at stuff, say “yes” as often as you can. Demo every game you’re invited to if it even looks a tad bit interesting. This is part of wandering the vendor hall early. You can play your favorite games anytime you want back home, so try out some new games to see if you can find any new favorites.

Plan out big purchases and get them out of the way early. Big here refers to both size of the game, and money spent. Gencon is an absolute black hole for time and money. If you don’t budget and plan, you’ll find yourself in a world of hurt. I like to go buy every game I know 100% I’m going to buy first thing on the first day (to make sure it doesn't run out too) and then drop it all off in my car. Lucky people can drop stuff off in their nearby hotel room.
Some real good tips. Don't forget to try to haggle on some prices. If you go in Sunday you can find some bargins on games you were on the edge.
